newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH files with US regulator on DFS bid. [CORRECTED 14:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: LVMH files with US regulator on DFS bid. [CORRECTED 14:30 GMT]

text.p: French luxury goods conglomerate LVMH has filed for clearance from the U.S. Federal Trade Commission for its proposed purchase of 59 percent of duty free chain DFS, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.

She said the filing was routine and declined to comment on speculation in newspapers that it might delay or endanger the deal, which is being contested by two minority shareholders of DFS. The quarrel has been put to an outside arbitrator under the terms of the DFS partnership agreement.
The spokeswoman said LVMH had not made public any target date for the closing of the deal.
"We don't know when the arbiter will give his decision," she told Reuters.

LVMH announced on October 30 that it had struck an agreement to buy 58.75 percent of San Francisco-based DFS. The agreement has been reported in newspapers as having a December 31 "walk-away" date allowing those shareholders who have agreed to sell to cancel the deal if it has not closed.
There have been no reports that the sellers want to back out.
(Corrects to show there are no reports sellers want to back out)
Rumours circulated in the Paris bourse on Monday that LVMH expected the deal to close by the end of the year, but the spokeswoman said that was pure speculation.
The FTC review normally lasts around a month.

Analysts and investors are sensitive to developments in the deal because of the DFS partners' quarrel and a report in The Wall Street Journal last month that Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co was considering an offer for DFS.
LVMH shares were unchanged at 1,268 francs at 1140 GMT in a slightly weaker stockmarket.
